item.title: Philippine Senate lowers threshold for conviction in VP Duterte's impeachment trial
item.description: The Philippine Senate, sitting as an impeachment court, on Wednesday lowered the number of votes needed to convict Vice President Sara Duterte, reducing the threshold prosecutors must clear to secure a guilty verdict.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Philippine Senate, sitting as an impeachment court, on Wednesday lowered the number of votes needed to convict Vice President [USN:L6N44X00V TEXT:"Sara Duterte"], reducing the threshold prosecutors must clear to secure a guilty verdict. The court ruled that only senator-judges able to participate in the trial should be counted when determining the threshold for conviction. Four of the 24 senator-judges have been unable to participate in the proceedings and cannot vote. The decision means prosecutors now need 14 votes for a conviction, instead of the 16 votes required when all 24 are taking part. Some senators had argued to keep the 16-vote threshold regardless of the four absences, which would have made it more challenging to convict Duterte. The [USN:L6N41P0K7 TEXT:"impeachment trial"] follows a [USN:L4N3EK0Y7 TEXT:"high-profile fallout"] between Duterte and her former ally and running mate President Ferdinand Marcos Jr and the outcome could shape the 2028 presidential election, which Duterte [USN:P8N3T403W TEXT:"intends to contest"]. Marcos is limited by the constitution to a single term in office and is expected to back a [USN:SPN431008 TEXT:"successor"]. Duterte, a frontrunner in early opinion polls, faces a ban from holding political office if convicted by the court and would be out of the presidential running. She stands [USN:L6N42W0PH TEXT:"accused"] of misusing public funds, amassing unexplained wealth and [USN:L4N3MU01O TEXT:"threatening"] the lives of Marcos, the first lady and a former House Speaker. Duterte denies wrongdoing. "This is the best chance to secure a conviction," Michael Henry Yusingco, a senior research fellow at the Ateneo Policy Center in Manila, said of the court's decision to lower the voting threshold.

item.title: España autoriza el proceso judicial de extradición de un donante propalestino a EEUU
item.description: España autorizó este martes que la solicitud de extradición presentada por Estados Unidos contra el donante propalestino James Cox Chambers pase a la fase judicial, a pesar de las protestas de los socios de la coalición de izquierdas del Gobierno, que sostienen que el caso tiene motivaciones políticas.
item.dc:creator: Victoria Waldersee
item.content:encoded: España autorizó este martes que la solicitud de extradición presentada por Estados Unidos contra el donante propalestino James Cox Chambers pase a la fase judicial, a pesar de las protestas de los socios de la coalición de izquierdas del Gobierno, que sostienen que el caso tiene motivaciones políticas. El caso es políticamente delicado para el Gobierno español liderado por los socialistas, cuya postura a favor de Palestina ha suscitado críticas por parte del Gobierno de Trump y ha contribuido a agravar las tensiones con Washington. Chambers, de 41 años, un multimillonario estadounidense heredero de un imperio mediático conocido como Fergie, fue detenido a petición de las autoridades estadounidenses el 10 de julio mientras estaba de vacaciones en Ibiza. Actualmente se encuentra en prisión preventiva en Madrid. Chambers, que se autodefine como antimperialista y comunista, ha abogado en entrevistas y en redes sociales por la destrucción de Estados Unidos. Recibió 250 millones de dólares tras desprenderse de su participación en el conglomerado mediático familiar, Cox Enterprises, en 2023, según su portavoz. Chambers ha donado más de un millón de dólares a causas humanitarias en Gaza y ha sufragado los gastos legales de algunos miembros del grupo activista Palestine Action, según su equipo jurídico. El grupo fue calificado como organización terrorista por Estados Unidos y Reino Unido por sus acciones, que incluyen ataques contra empresas de defensa vinculadas a Israel mediante el bloqueo de entrada a edificios y el uso de pintura en aerosol. Estados Unidos no ha detallado públicamente los cargos contra Chambers. Su equipo jurídico afirma que incluyen blanqueo de capitales y conspiración para cometer alteración del orden público. El Departamento de Justicia de Estados Unidos se ha negado a hacer comentarios sobre los cargos. El caso ha suscitado un gran interés entre figuras propalestinas, y 150 destacados activistas y personalidades, entre ellos Richard Gere, Greta Thunberg y Fatima Bhutto, han firmado una carta en la que instan a España a no seguir adelante con el proceso de extradición. Tanto los abogados de Chambers como Sumar, el socio menor de la coalición de los socialistas, afirman que la falta de pruebas disponibles públicamente sugiere que se le está persiguiendo por sus opiniones políticas. Según la legislación española, la extradición no puede llevarse a cabo si se determina que la solicitud tiene motivaciones políticas. "Sentaría un precedente alarmante en toda Europa si España permitiera que la Administración Trump criminalizara la prestación de ayuda humanitaria vital al pueblo palestino y la defensa de sus derechos", afirmó el abogado de Chambers, Baltasar Garzón, quien ha presentado una solicitud de asilo para Chambers en España. La portavoz del Gobierno, Elma Saiz, señaló que la decisión de dar curso al caso era "puramente procedimental", y añadió que el Consejo de Ministros tomaría la decisión definitiva una vez concluido el proceso judicial. La fecha de la vista se fijará en las próximas semanas, informó un portavoz del tribunal.

item.title: Catalonia's far-right surge divides independence camp as migration fears grow
item.description: Almost a decade after Catalonia's failed independence bid, a growing number of voters are shifting their focus from secession to issues such as immigration and crime, fuelling the rise of the far-right separatist Aliança Catalana.
item.dc:creator: Joan Faus
item.content:encoded: Almost a decade after Catalonia's failed [USN:KCN1C60Y5 TEXT:"independence bid"], a growing number of voters are shifting their focus from secession to issues such as immigration and crime, fuelling the rise of the far-right separatist Aliança Catalana. The party, which draws much of its support from working- and middle-class voters in rural areas outside Barcelona, has surged in the polls and now trails only Spain's ruling Socialists ahead of Catalonia's next election in 2028. While Aliança says it would seek to break away from Madrid unilaterally if it won power in the wealthy northeastern region, its message is focused far more on curbing immigration and improving public safety. Its growing influence is reshaping Catalan politics. Earlier this month, riot police prevented violent clashes between Aliança supporters and left-wing separatists in Barcelona, overshadowing Catalonia's September 11 national day celebrations, which have historically drawn large pro-independence crowds. The episode highlighted divisions within [USN:S8N3ZT0BM TEXT:"the separatist movement"], potentially complicating efforts to form a coalition to unseat the region's ruling Socialist Party. Traditional pro-independence parties have ruled out governing agreements with Aliança. As its support has grown, other separatist parties have adopted more conservative positions, including lobbying Madrid to let the region restrict migration. The party's appeal cuts across Catalonia's traditional political divides. Much of its support comes from voters who previously backed the separatist centre-right Junts or the far-right, staunchly anti-independence Vox, according to a Catalan government survey published in July. STRAIGHT-TALKING LEADER Aliança's rise has been driven largely by its outspoken leader, Silvia Orriols, 41, who studied to become a librarian and comes from a middle-class farming family. Orriols told Reuters her party was tapping into frustration with established politicians and concerns that immigration was diluting Catalan identity. "People have regained hope and drive to fight for the restoration of the Catalan state, to implement policies aimed at preserving our identity," said Orriols, who frequently invokes Catalonia's history in her speeches. She said far-right Alternative for Germany's [USN:L8N44X04E TEXT:"victory"] in Saxony-Anhalt state earlier this month showed that "Europe is awakening". "We Europeans are shielding ourselves in order to survive," she said. Aliança rose to prominence in 2023 after Orriols won a local election in Ripoll. Her anti-Muslim message gained traction in the mountainous town where most of the Moroccan-born perpetrators of the [USN:KCN1AY18Y TEXT:"2017 Barcelona terror attacks"] had lived. The party entered Catalonia's parliament a year later with two seats. Since then, it has grown from 3.8% to 16.7% of voter intentions for the next regional election, according to a poll published by El Mundo newspaper this month. It was 2.6 percentage points ahead of fellow separatist party ERC. Eloi Radovan, whose family traditionally backed left-wing pro-independence parties like ERC, is among those who have shifted their support to Aliança. "I feel betrayed," said Radovan, 19, referring to how parties like ERC and Junts failed to follow through on the [USN:L8N2QQ1LB TEXT:"2017 referendum"] in which Catalans voted in favour of independence. He also criticised their cooperation with Socialist Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez. He supports Aliança's call for a total ban on migration because, he said, "Catalonia is increasingly becoming less Catalan". Junts is seeking to counter Aliança's appeal by presenting itself as a more pragmatic centrist alternative while offering its own proposals on migration and security. Two senior Junts officials told Reuters they viewed Aliança's plans as unrealistic and discriminatory. CHANGING CONCERNS The party's gains have coincided with shifting priorities among Catalan voters. Affordable housing, migration and crime topped the list of concerns in the July survey. Two years earlier, political dissatisfaction and Catalonia's relationship with the rest of Spain ranked highest. "The (2017) independence push was driven by economic anxiety, whereas Aliança responds to demographic anxiety," said historian Joan Esculies. Aliança's rise is "an expression of frustration at the lack of a viable path towards independence and a cry born of fear as new waves of immigration pose a greater threat to (Catalan) language," he said. Yet support for independence has remained resilient despite divisions within the movement and the loss of the regional presidency in 2024 after a decade in power. The July survey showed 45% backing independence, down from a peak of 49% in 2017. Critics say Aliança is exploiting those frustrations rather than offering solutions. The party offers no real solutions and other separatists must combat its "xenophobic, racist discourse of exclusion," said left-wing separatist Hug Lucchetti, 45, during this month's protests. "The independence movement is alive," he said. "New ranks of activists continue to emerge."

item.title: L'administration US va accueillir en priorité des Afrikaners en tant que réfugiés
item.description: L'administration Trump prévoit de prendre en charge un maximum de 17.500 réfugiés, "principalement" des membres de la communauté des Afrikaners d'Afrique du Sud, au cours des douze prochains mois, selon un document transmis mardi au Congrès américain.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: L'administration Trump prévoit de prendre en charge un maximum de 17.500 réfugiés, "principalement" des membres de la communauté des Afrikaners d'Afrique du Sud, au cours des douze prochains mois, selon un document transmis mardi au Congrès américain. Le président Donald Trump a affirmé que les membres de la communauté Afrikaners faisaient l'objet de persécutions, des accusations rejetées par Pretoria. Donald Trump a suspendu toutes les demandes d'asile à son arrivée à la Maison blanche en janvier 2025 avant de lancer une procédure pour accueillir des membres de la communauté des Afrikaners. Le document transmis mardi par le département d'Etat à des membres du Congrès indique qu'il "anticipe que les Afrikaners d'Afrique du Sud s'intégreront pleinement aux Etats-Unis de manière à préserver les ressources des contribuables au profit des citoyens américains". Des quelque 3.000 réfugiés admis aux Etats-Unis durant l'année fiscale qui se termine le 30 septembre 2026, seuls trois n'étaient pas originaires d'Afrique du Sud, selon des données du département d'Etat. Plus de 100.000 réfugiés originaires de dizaines de pays avaient été accueilli aux Etats-Unis en 2024, sous l'administration Biden.

item.title: Trump's diesel export dilemma — Good politics, bad economics
item.description: Soaring fuel costs are increasing pressure on US President Donald Trump to curb diesel exports ahead of November's midterm elections. But what may seem like an easy fix could unleash a chain reaction that ultimately leaves American consumers and the global economy worse off.
item.dc:creator: Ron Bousso
item.content:encoded: Soaring fuel costs are [USN:L6N45D0NV TEXT:"increasing pressure"] on US President Donald Trump to curb diesel exports ahead of November's midterm elections . But what may seem like an easy fix could unleash a chain reaction that ultimately leaves American consumers and the global economy worse off. Surging energy prices since the start of the Iran war in late February are [USN:L6N4590YX TEXT:"setting off alarm bells"] in the White House. While politically sensitive gasoline prices remain elevated at nearly $4.50 a gallon, attention in recent weeks has shifted to diesel, which has climbed to a record $6.50 a gallon, squeezing trucking, [USN:L6N457127 TEXT:"farming"], manufacturing and other sectors that rely on the fuel to keep goods moving. Trump on Tuesday said he [USN:SPN45A01C TEXT:"backed the idea"] of a ban on diesel exports, which some [USN:L1N45D0Y8 TEXT:"Republican lawmakers"], particularly those representing agricultural states, have called for. US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the administration was examining whether a full or partial ban would work. Some senior administration officials, including Energy Secretary Chris Wright and Interior Secretary Doug Burgum, have in recent weeks nevertheless [USN:L1N4560TC TEXT:"expressed doubts"] about whether such a move would work. Yet with fuel costs becoming a growing political liability and midterm elections fast approaching, the temptation to seek a politically popular “quick fix” may prove difficult to resist – especially as the president’s [USN:L6N45D0NV TEXT:"poll numbers sink"] to new lows. Trump has the authority to restrict exports temporarily under emergency powers. He would certainly not be the first president to intervene – or contemplate intervening – in energy markets. The US prohibited crude oil exports for four decades following the 1973 oil crisis, while former President Joe Biden's administration considered restricting diesel exports in 2022 after Russia's invasion of Ukraine sent fuel markets into turmoil. The trouble is that a diesel export ban would likely aggravate the very problem it is designed to solve. KEEPING UP WITH THE JONES ACT The current [USN:L6N450107 TEXT:"fuel crunch"] is almost entirely conflict-driven. The Middle East and Russia used to account collectively for roughly a fifth of global seaborne exports of diesel. But the Iran war and the resulting disruption to shipping through the [USN:L4N45E08Z TEXT:"Strait of Hormuz"] have removed a sizeable portion of global refining capacity and diesel supplies. This squeeze [USN:L8N4391IZ TEXT:"intensified in July"] when Russia, traditionally one of the world's largest diesel exporters, halted shipments following months of Ukrainian drone attacks that crippled large parts of its refining sector. Half of Russia's six top diesel-producing refineries significantly cut back or completely [USN:L8N4570EX TEXT:"halted output in September"] due to damage sustained in drone attacks, Reuters reported. The Trump administration has already tried several measures to ease domestic prices, with limited success. In March, Washington issued a waiver to the century-old [USN:SPN43H00L TEXT:"Jones Act"], which requires cargo shipped between US ports to travel on vessels that are US-built, US-owned, US-flagged and largely US-crewed. The waiver, which expires on November 15, was designed to make it easier for refiners along the US Gulf Coast refining hub to supply diesel to consuming regions on the East and West coasts. But the results have been negligible. Trump has also sought relief abroad by encouraging Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskiy to [USN:S8N41C0VK TEXT:"halt strikes"] on Russian energy infrastructure. Those efforts have produced little progress, with attacks [USN:L8N45D1DG TEXT:"continuing"] in recent days. US DIESEL SURPLUS The US has emerged as one of the few suppliers capable of helping fill the gap created by the loss of Middle Eastern and Russian fuel, taking advantage of huge margins in the process. Total US oil exports have surged by over 20% since March, compared with the 2025 average to 9 million barrels per day (bpd), according to Kpler. That role, however, has come at a cost. Those enormous exports are limiting the amount of product available domestically. US diesel inventories have fallen to their lowest level for this time of year in more than four decades and stand about 13% below last year's levels. The decline is especially concerning because stockpiles would normally be building ahead of autumn refinery maintenance and the winter heating season. The prospect of entering winter with unusually tight inventories has reinforced calls for an export ban. At first glance, the idea appears compelling. US refiners produced almost 5 million bpd of diesel last year, while domestic consumption was 3.9 million bpd. But that apparent surplus is precisely why a ban would backfire. Modern refining systems are designed to serve both domestic and international markets simultaneously. Gulf Coast refiners optimise operations based on global price signals, moving diesel, gasoline and jet fuel to whichever market values them most highly. Initially, an export ban would direct more fuel into domestic markets and storage tanks, temporarily depressing prices. Once those inventories filled, however, refiners would have little choice but to reduce processing rates because they would no longer be able to sell surplus diesel abroad. The consequence would be lower production of not only diesel but also of gasoline, jet fuel and other products. In other words, a diesel export ban would not just fail to create more fuel, it could eventually discourage production. That reality helps explain why both the Biden and Trump administrations have approached the idea cautiously. The political risks extend beyond the pump. Restricting exports could undermine America's reputation as a reliable energy supplier just as Washington seeks to promote its energy dominance agenda. It would also strain relations with allies and customers, particularly in Europe and Asia, that have become increasingly dependent on US fuel. The case against a diesel export ban thus seems pretty clear-cut, but whether the administration can withstand the political pressure to impose one is far less obvious. (The opinions expressed here are those of Ron Bousso , a columnist for Reuters.) Enjoying this column? item.title: Darkest before dawn? Funds mull return to bonds
item.description: A grueling year of war, oil shocks and re-ignited inflation has hammered government bonds everywhere. Yet with higher US interest rates now a reality, some investors believe this is finally the moment to pounce on bonds offering yields not seen in decades.
item.dc:creator: Mike Dolan
item.content:encoded: A grueling year of war, oil shocks and re-ignited inflation has hammered government bonds everywhere. Yet with higher US interest rates [USN:L6N4570XW TEXT:"now a reality"], some investors believe this is finally the moment to pounce on bonds offering yields not seen in decades. We've been here many times before, of course, and speculative attempts to bet again on a turn in this six-year-long bear market in bonds have caused havoc for many punters. For investors in Treasury exchange-traded funds (ETFs), it's been particularly painful, with the iShares US Treasury ETF down 3.6% year-to-date and on course for the second-worst annual loss in its 14-year history — second only to the oil and interest-rate shock following Russia's invasion of Ukraine in 2022. Long-term Group of Seven (G7) government bonds, as measured by Bloomberg's catch-all index, have now almost halved in price since the pandemic lockdowns of 2020 — an average annual loss of about 9%. But each historic milestone in rising debt yields tempts fixed-income managers to reconsider their exposure, and many are once again looking to extend the maturity and duration of their holdings. With yields on US and G7 10- to 30-year government bonds hitting their highest in decades this month, the latest wave of central bank rate hikes may curb any re-emergence of long-term inflation expectations. "We think that the worst of the big bond bear market of 2026 may be behind us at this particular moment," RBC BlueBay's fixed-income chief investment officer, Mark Dowding, told Reuters on Tuesday. In the wake of the first Federal Reserve rate hike in three years last week, he added that he was taking a more constructive view of duration — essentially long-dated debt most sensitive to interest rate moves. Dowding's rationale was that the violent swing in Fed rate expectations in futures markets in recent months from a dovish, [USN:L6N44Z0M5 TEXT:"politically tinged"] view had hurt speculative players on the wrong side of the trade and pushed the pendulum too far in the other direction. The market's pricing of as many as [USN:L6N45D0VX TEXT:"three more rate hikes"] through the middle of next year, the clearing out of loss-making speculative bets and what he saw as relatively benign inflation trends all pointed to a tentative return to battered bonds, Dowding said. That view was likely to apply equally to other central banks and G7 bond markets, Dowding said. JUICY FRUIT? That macro take chimed with Goldman Sachs chief economist Jan Hatzius, who on Tuesday reckoned the Fed's surprisingly hawkish stance would still fall short of the more aggressive market pricing. Even with one more hike in the arsenal this year, Hatzius wrote that Goldman still expected soft underlying inflation trends would see the Fed reverse those hikes by late 2027. "The repricing of monetary policy expectations explains most of the surge in government bond yields. Under our forecast that some of this repricing will reverse, our rates strategists see long-term yields also coming down modestly," the Goldman economist wrote. And Apollo chief economist Torsten Slok also pointed out on Tuesday that nominal yields across the fixed-income universe were starting to look "juicy". "After a decade of reaching for yield in a zero-rate world, investors no longer have to take outsized risk to generate income," he wrote. "Even if yields rise further from here, current levels in high-quality fixed income are already attractive." For mixed-asset portfolios, such yields still do not match the AI-driven equity gains on offer today. But with 10-year Treasury yields around 5% and earnings yields for the S&P 500 (.SPX) only a sliver above that, bonds now give equities a good run for their money. Even if the speculative bond bets from earlier in the year have been flushed out, the positioning of asset managers in bonds has not been this light in more than four years. According to the latest Bank of America global funds survey released on the eve of this month's Fed hike, a net 48% of investors were underweight bonds, the most extreme reading since May 2022. The current mix of higher yields, light positioning and hopes for softer inflation is tempting many asset managers. But then the arguments for returning to bonds have been many and wrong for at least a couple of years. Much will hinge on the most basic input to the macro view: precisely how strong the underlying growth trend is in the US and around the world. If growth is accelerating rather than slowing, then the hawkish take on the Fed and other central banks may not be so wide of the mark after all. That then spins into the scale of the AI buildout, not least with its corporate-debt implications, and the longevity of the energy inflation heat from two major wars still raging. These are significant uncertainties for any major investment play, but the re-emerging bond bulls are relying more on the fact that yields are much higher and bear markets don't last forever. Whether bonds can start to perform without the stock market rolling over — with bonds traditionally at their best when equities are under pressure — is an altogether more difficult question. (The opinions expressed here are those of Mike Dolan , a columnist for Reuters.) Enjoying this column? item.title: Sri Lanka economy resilient but risks remain tilted to downside, IMF says
item.description: The International Monetary Fund said on Wednesday that Sri Lanka's economy continues to show resilience amid successive shocks but is still facing risks tilted to the downside, as its staff concluded a visit to the South Asian island nation.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The International Monetary Fund said on Wednesday that Sri Lanka's economy continues to show resilience amid successive shocks but is still facing risks tilted to the downside, as its staff concluded a visit to the South Asian island nation. The island nation, backed by a $2.9 billion programme, is clawing its way out of a 2022 economic upheaval triggered by severe shortage of dollars. The IMF review comes as Sri Lanka looks to maintain growth and contain high inflation caused by soaring energy prices that have prevailed since the Gulf conflict began seven months ago. Sri Lanka's economy continues to show resilience amid successive shocks but is still facing risks tilted to the downside, the IMF said in a statement. The key priorities remain development of a strong medium-term revenue strategy and administration, upholding energy cost recovery, and executing capital investment, it said. The lender suggested it would be prudent to maintain the 5 percent inflation target and the prevailing accountability band, adding that commitment to prudent policies and reforms was also critical to safeguard macroeconomic stability. "Shifting from stabilization to transformation requires sustained momentum on structural reforms to reduce poverty and lift living standards through strong and inclusive growth," it said. The IMF approved a $700 million double tranche to Sri Lanka under the programme in May to help bolster its reserves, and has predicted the country could grow by 3% this year. The country, which imports all its fuel, however, is struggling to cope with the rise in energy costs. It introduced fuel rationing, steeply increased prices, and declared Wednesdays as public holidays from early March in an attempt to use fuel judiciously.

item.title: 習主席は「偉大な指導者」、マスク氏がインタビューで称賛
item.description: [北京 ２３日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[北京 ２３日 ロイター] - 米電気自動車（ＥＶ）大手テスラのイーロン・マスク最高経営責任者（ＣＥＯ）は２３日、中国国営中央テレビ（ＣＣＴＶ）のインタビューで、中国の習近平国家主席を「偉大な指導者」と称賛した。

「習主席の在任期間中、中国は目覚ましい繁栄を遂げた」とし、新たに建設された建物やインフラに進歩が見て取れると指摘。「街を歩くだけでも、一般の中国国民の生活水準が向上していることは一目瞭然だ」と語った。

習氏は２４日にトランプ米大統領と会談する予定で、マスク氏はホワイトハウスで開かれる夕食会に他の米企業ＣＥＯらと共に出席するとみられている。

マスク氏は上海にあるテスラ最大の製造拠点にも言及し、現地チームを「非常に有能かつ勤勉で、信頼できる」と評価した。

「テスラの上海工場は宝のような存在で、実際に行ったことがある人ならわかると思うが、実に美しい」と述べた。

同氏は以前、宇宙企業スペースＸとの合併を視野にテスラの中国事業を分離する可能性があるとの憶測を否定している。

item.title: Trump y Lee avanzan en cooperación estratégica y diálogo sobre Corea del Norte
item.description: El presidente surcoreano, Lee Jae-myung, y el presidente de EEUU, Donald Trump, celebraron los "importantes avances" logrados en las conversaciones sobre proyectos de inversión estratégica durante una reunión de 30 minutos celebrada al margen de la Asamblea General de la ONU, informó este miércoles la oficina presidencial de Seúl.
item.dc:creator: Kyu-Seok Shim, Heejin Kim
item.content:encoded: El presidente surcoreano, Lee Jae-myung, y el presidente de EEUU, Donald Trump, celebraron los "importantes avances" logrados en las conversaciones sobre proyectos de inversión estratégica durante una reunión de 30 minutos celebrada al margen de la Asamblea General de la ONU, informó este miércoles la oficina presidencial de Seúl. La reunión tuvo lugar después de que el Ministerio de Industria de Corea del Sur informara el martes a los legisladores sobre los planes de ejecución del paquete de inversión de 350.000 millones de dólares entre ambos países, que incluye un proyecto de central eléctrica de gas en Texas identificado como una posible primera inversión, así como posibles inversiones en energía nuclear y un proyecto de GNL en Alaska. "Los dos líderes celebraron los importantes avances logrados en las conversaciones sobre proyectos de inversión estratégicos entre ambos países", dijo el asesor de Seguridad Nacional, Wi Sung-lac, en una rueda de prensa. Según la hoja informativa conjunta publicada tras su cumbre del pasado mes de noviembre, Lee y Trump también acordaron profundizar en la cooperación y continuar las conversaciones sobre el enriquecimiento y el reprocesamiento de combustible nuclear, los submarinos de propulsión nuclear, la construcción naval y la transferencia del control operativo en tiempo de guerra (OPCON, por sus siglas en inglés) de EEUU a Corea del Sur, señaló Wi. Trump también reafirmó su voluntad de entablar un diálogo con Corea del Norte, señaló Wi, y ambos líderes acordaron mantenerse en estrecha comunicación para impulsar el proceso de paz. Lee también señaló que la cumbre entre EEUU y China prevista para el jueves sería importante para la evolución de la región, incluidas las relaciones entre Corea del Sur y China, y expresó su esperanza de que la reunión fuera un éxito, según Wi. La Casa Blanca no hizo comentarios inmediatos sobre la reunión entre Trump y Lee. El secretario de Estado de EEUU, Marco Rubio, pidió el viernes la rápida ejecución de los compromisos de inversión de Corea del Sur durante una reunión con el ministro de Asuntos Exteriores surcoreano, Cho Hyun, según el Departamento de Estado. HABLARON DE COREA DEL NORTE Y DE GOLF El miércoles por la mañana, Lee dijo ante la Asamblea General de la ONU que Seúl apoyaría los esfuerzos para reactivar el diálogo con Corea del Norte y trabajaría en favor de un marco de paz duradero, al tiempo que buscaría un respaldo internacional más amplio para dichos esfuerzos. Un alto cargo de la Presidencia dijo por separado a los medios de comunicación surcoreanos que Lee le había dicho a Trump que esperaba que el presidente de EEUU ayudara a impulsar el diálogo con Corea del Norte, a lo que Trump respondió que así lo haría. El alto cargo señaló que Trump también comentó que mantenía una buena relación con el líder norcoreano Kim Jong-un, aunque no había indicios de que se estuviera produciendo ningún contacto específico en estos momentos, informaron los medios de comunicación. Añadió que Lee y Trump también dedicaron un tiempo considerable a debatir la transferencia del OPCON, y que Trump llegó a comprender mejor la posición de Seúl. La parte estadounidense hizo hincapié en la necesidad de cumplir las condiciones requeridas y completar el proceso lo antes posible, según estas informaciones. La parte surcoreana esbozó planes para aumentar el gasto en defensa, al tiempo que expresó su deseo de acelerar las conversaciones sobre los planes de Seúl para desarrollar submarinos de propulsión nuclear, según el alto cargo. Ambas partes acordaron celebrar consultas de seguimiento sobre los distintos temas en Washington lo antes posible, según las informaciones. Según se citó al alto cargo, los avances en las negociaciones sobre las inversiones surcoreanas en proyectos estadounidenses contribuyeron a allanar el camino para la cumbre, cuya celebración no se había previsto inicialmente. Los dos líderes habían sido informados sobre las negociaciones y acogieron con satisfacción los avances, pero aún se estaban debatiendo los detalles del paquete y la forma en que se anunciaría, según el alto cargo. "El marco general está casi completo", dijo, según se citó. Trump planteó la posibilidad de jugar al golf con Lee, quien sugirió que ambos podrían hacerlo en el marco de la cumbre del G20 que se celebrará en Miami en diciembre, según el alto cargo. Ambos ya habían hablado de jugar al golf durante su encuentro en la cumbre del G7 celebrada en Francia en junio.

item.title: Shooting at South Africa house party kills 11, injures three
item.description: Three armed men opened fire on guests at a house party in a township south of the South African city of Durban, killing at least 11 and injuring three, police said on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Three armed men opened fire on guests at a house party in a township south of the South African city of Durban, killing at least 11 and injuring three, police said on Wednesday. A woman believed to be pregnant and 13 men were among those attending Tuesday's party in the township of KwaMakhutha in KwaZulu-Natal province, police said. "Ten victims, including the woman, died at the scene and four were taken to hospital, were one of them succumbed to gunshot injuries," they added in a statement. The motive for the attack is not known, but police said initial investigation showed some of the victims were known to authorities, without giving details. South Africa has one of the world's highest murder rates, averaging about 60 a day.

item.title: India business activity rebounds in September to 3-month high, PMI shows
item.description: India's business growth accelerated in September on stronger demand in both manufacturing and services, a preliminary survey showed, though weaker export momentum and more subdued hiring tempered the upbeat picture.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: India's business growth accelerated in September on stronger demand in both manufacturing and services, a preliminary survey showed, though weaker export momentum and more subdued hiring tempered the upbeat picture. HSBC's flash India Composite Purchasing Managers' Index (PMI) rose to 56.5 from August's 54.3, its highest since June and back above its long-run average. It exceeded the Reuters poll median forecast of 54.4. Readings above 50 indicate expansion. But the rebound did not reverse the quarter's broader slowdown. Based on September's preliminary reading, the composite index averaged 55.1 this quarter, down from 58.2 in April-June, suggesting softer growth in Asia's third-largest economy after a [USN:L4N44S0T4 TEXT:"forecast-beating"] 7.8% expansion last quarter. The manufacturing PMI climbed to 55.7 from 52.8, its highest in seven months, as output and new orders grew faster. Goods producers also resumed hiring after a marginal reduction in August. The services index rose to 55.8 from 54.1. However, new exports increased at the slowest pace in 33 months, offsetting a modest pickup in manufacturing exports and dragging overall export growth lower. Hiring in the services sector also lost momentum. Overall input-cost inflation eased to its lowest since January, driven by services, offering businesses some relief. Yet selling-price inflation was broadly unchanged, suggesting consumers saw scant relief from rising prices. Business confidence about the coming year rose to a four-month high.

item.title: Indian court rejects Adani plea that duty-free shops are beyond domestic laws
item.description: An Indian court has ruled that goods sold at duty-free shops are not immune from domestic laws, dealing a blow to the Adani Group's airport sales of nicotine pouches, which New Delhi calls illegal and regards as drugs.
item.dc:creator: Aditya Kalra
item.content:encoded: An Indian court has ruled that goods sold at duty-free shops are not immune from domestic laws, dealing a blow to the Adani Group's airport sales of nicotine pouches, which New Delhi calls illegal and regards as drugs. In a case widely seen as setting a precedent on duty-free sales, Adani in April challenged Indian authorities who said its Mumbai international airport shops [USN:L4N4380LR TEXT:"illegally stocked and sold"] nicotine pouches, one of the world's fastest-growing nicotine products, which remain unapproved in India. Billionaire Gautam Adani's group manages eight airports in India and has an ambitious $11 billion expansion plan, including for duty-free shops, to capitalise on the growing demand for air travel. While Indian authorities told the court that stocking nicotine pouches was a [USN:L4N43C0OH TEXT:""substantive violation""] of drug laws and a "serious public health risk", Adani denied any wrongdoing. Adani argued in court that shops in international departure areas are outside the reach of domestic regulations as they sit beyond India's territorial jurisdiction. The High Court in Mumbai disagreed in an order issued late Tuesday. "Such goods would be subject to the law of the land and would be governed by the regulatory regime in force even if the transaction takes place in the DFS (duty free shops), beyond the customs barrier," the order said. "The domestic regulatory regime will apply in full force to such goods brought into the DFS within the Indian territorial jurisdiction," it added. Adani Group did not immediately respond to Reuters requests for comment. In its court submissions, Adani also argued that nicotine pouches are "not a drug" and a "recent innovation", and attract no scrutiny under Indian laws - a position New Delhi disagreed with. The court said it could not answer that question at this stage and instead said Adani was free to make representations before Indian drug regulators, with supporting material, and the regulator can decide that on its merits.

item.title: Tigers' Justin Verlander expected to make final career start Saturday
item.description: The Detroit Tigers may be out of playoff contention, but Saturday's penultimate game of the season is expected to be a tough ticket to get in the Motor City.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: The Detroit Tigers may be out of playoff contention, but Saturday's penultimate game of the season is expected to be a tough ticket to get in the Motor City. Tigers manager A.J. Hinch said Tuesday that Justin Verlander will make the final start of his career Saturday against the Pittsburgh Pirates. "Barring any sort of major issue, and I don't see one coming, he's going to be all set for Saturday," Hinch said. Verlander confirmed the news to reporters Tuesday, saying, "It doesn't need to be a perfect game for me to be able to stay out there. If I'm able to continue to be healthy and I feel good." "I don't just want to go out there and do the one inning or come out and wave. I would like to toe the rubber one more time in a competitive way and try to win the Detroit Tigers a ballgame." The future Hall of Fame right-hander has made just one appearance this season, a March 30 start against the Diamondbacks in Arizona, where he went 3 2/3 innings, gave up five runs, and took the loss. The 43-year-old has spent the rest of the season to this point sidelined with hip and hamstring injuries. He announced shortly before the All-Star break that this would be his last season, after he was named to the American League team as a "legend pick." The team announced earlier this month that they would host a celebration weekend for Verlander on Friday and Saturday. Verlander is 266-159 with a 3.33 ERA in 556 career games (all starts) with the Tigers (2005-17, 2026), Houston Astros (2017-20, 2022-24), New York Mets (2023) and San Francisco Giants (2025). He leads all active pitchers in wins and ranks eighth all-time in strikeouts (3,554). "He's going to give his best shot to have as close to a normal game as he can. ... he's going to have to make pitches, and we're going to have to play defense and things like that," Hinch said. Verlander said his immediate task is simply getting to Saturday healthy. "I'm like, ‘All right, just don't do anything stupid between now and Saturday, and we should be good,'" he said Tuesday. "There's a lot of emotion, but also some angst to go pitch. And obviously I want go pitch well, so I'm trying to do everything I possibly can to allow that to happen." Saturday will mark Verlander's first start at Comerica Park in a Tigers uniform since Aug. 20, 2017, 11 days before Detroit traded him to Houston. --Field Level Media

item.title: ＭＬＢ＝村上が今季33号、ドジャース佐々木は復帰し救援登板
item.description: ［２２日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［２２日　ロイター］ - 米大リーグ（ＭＬＢ）は２２日、各地で試合を行い、ホワイトソックスの村上宗隆内野手がロイヤルズ戦に「４番・一塁」で出場し、今季３３号をマークした。

村上は七回に右翼へ２ランを放ち、３打数１安打、２打点、２四死球、１三振。ホワイトソックスは１４─１１で勝利し、残り５試合でア・リーグ中地区首位ガーディアンズとの１ゲーム差をキープし、プレーオフ進出へのマジックを「３」とした。

メッツの千賀滉大投手はレンジャース戦の九回に４番手として登板。１回を無安打無失点、１死球、２奪三振とし、今季８セーブ目を挙げた。チームは６─３で勝利した。

負傷者リスト（ＩＬ）から復帰したドジャースの佐々木朗希投手は、パドレス戦の四回に４番手として登板。１回を２安打無失点、２三振で抑え、チームの７─０での勝利に貢献した。

カブスの今永昇太投手はマーリンズ戦に先発し、５回を４安打１失点、１死球、７奪三振の内容で勝敗つかず。チームは延長十二回に６失点を喫し、２─８で敗れた。同僚の鈴木誠也外野手は「２番・右翼」で出場し、６打数２安打、１三振だった。

エンゼルスの菊池雄星投手はアスレチックス戦に先発し、５回１／３を投げて７安打２失点、１四球、２奪三振。勝利投手の権利を持って降板したが、後続が打たれチームは７─９で敗れた。

item.title: EFG International resolves Kuwait legal case
item.description: EFG International has reached a final settlement with the Public Institution for Social Security (PIFSS) of Kuwait related to civil proceedings in the UK, the Swiss private bank said on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: EFG International (EFGN.S) has reached a final settlement with the Public Institution for Social Security (PIFSS) of Kuwait related to civil proceedings in the UK, the Swiss private bank said on Wednesday. Kuwait's public pension fund [USN:L8N3Q011E TEXT:"had accused"] asset manager Man Group (EMG.L) , EFG and others of laundering bribes paid to its late director. EFG, which has already recorded a provision to cover the case, said the settlement will result in a marginal additional impact of about 5 million Swiss francs ($6.09 million)to its net profit in the second half of 2026. The settlement removes all legacy litigation risk for EFG related to the claims at issue in the UK proceedings, which related to events between 1995 and 2012, it added. ($1 = 0.8214 Swiss francs)

item.title: L'UE reconduit les sanctions russes sauf pour les milliardaires Alicher Ousmanov et Mikhaïl Fridman
item.description: Les membres de l'Union européenne ont prolongé de trois ans les sanctions contre près de 3.000 entreprises et individus russes mais en ont exempté deux milliardaires proches de Moscou à la demande de la France et du Luxembourg, ont déclaré mardi des diplomates européens.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Les membres de l'Union européenne ont prolongé de trois ans les sanctions contre près de 3.000 entreprises et individus russes mais en ont exempté deux milliardaires proches de Moscou à la demande de la France et du Luxembourg, ont déclaré mardi des diplomates européens. Jusqu'à présent, ces sanctions, prises à la suite de la guerre déclenchée en février 2022 par la Russie contre l'Ukraine, étaient prolongées tous les six mois. Mais en échange d'une prolongation de trois ans, les diplomates européens avaient conclu un accord de principe pour ôter de la liste de sanctions Alicher Ousmanov, un homme d'affaires russo-ouzbek, et l'oligarque russe Mikhaïl Fridman. Prenant nombre de membres de l'UE par surprise, la France avait plaidé la cause du premier. Le Luxembourg avait ensuite plaidé en faveur du second. Réagissant à la décision de l'Union européenne, le ministre des Affaires Etrangères ukrainien Andriy Sybiha l'a qualifiée de "honteuse et injustifiable". "Moscou doit se réjouir : la Russie a obtenu ce qu'elle voulait : un sentiment d'impunité, l'humiliation de l'UE et la division entre les Européens", a-t-il dit sur la plate-forme X. Dans la matinée, certains pays, dont la Lettonie, se sont encore dits opposés à cet accord de principe. La reconduction de sanctions doit être approuvée par un vote unanime. Après que la Lettonie s'est finalement abstenue dans le vote sur les sanctions, le Premier ministre letton Andris Kulbergs a dit qu'Emmanuel Macron avait accepté d'ouvrir des [USN:L8N45E18G TEXT:"discussions"] avec le pays balte pour qu'il rejoigne l'initiative de "dissuasion nucléaire avancée" lancée par la France.

item.title: Japan PM says she had 'timely' discussion with Trump ahead of his Xi summit
item.description: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said on Wednesday she had a "timely" discussion about China with US President Donald Trump ahead of his planned summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said on Wednesday she had a "timely" discussion about China with US President Donald Trump ahead of his planned summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday. "Japan considers it important that US-China relations contribute to the stability of the international community, including Japan," Takaichi said at a press conference in New York after meeting Trump on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly. Takaichi did not give details of what she and Trump discussed with regard to China. Japan and other [USN:L8N4570FX TEXT:"US allies in Asia are concerned"] that Trump could soften Washington's support for Taiwan in return for an economic deal with Xi. Takaichi's meeting with Trump was an opportunity for Japan to influence the president ahead of his sitdown with the Chinese leader. Xi is [USN:L1N45E095 TEXT:"expected to press Trump"] to halt arms sales to Taiwan when they meet, sources told Reuters earlier. Beijing views the democratically governed island as its own territory and is stepping up military activity around Taiwan. The island also lies close to Japan and Takaichi last year angered China after she said Tokyo could deploy its defence forces should any military action aimed at Taiwan also threaten its territory.

item.title: Roche proposes former Takeda CEO for board seat
item.description: Roche on Wednesday said it was proposing Christoph Weber, the former CEO of Takeda Pharmaceuticals , for election to the Swiss company's board of directors at its AGM next March.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Roche (ROPC.S) on Wednesday said it was proposing Christoph Weber, the former CEO of Takeda Pharmaceuticals (4502.T) , for election to the Swiss company's board of directors at its AGM next March. "Christophe's intimate knowledge of the healthcare industry and his broad leadership experience will further strengthen our Board," said Roche Chairman Severin Schwan in a statement.

item.title: EXCLUSIVE-アンソロピック、医療ＡＩ普及へ提携 中低所得国に提供
item.description:
Nancy Lapid
[２２日 ロイター] - 人工知能（ＡＩ）開発企業アンソロピックと医療情報プラットフォームの...
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
EXCLUSIVE-アンソロピック、医療ＡＩ普及へ提携　中低所得国に提供 14:10 配信

写真はアンソロピックのロゴ。２０２６年６月撮影。REUTERS/Dado Ruvic/Illustration

Nancy Lapid

[２２日 ロイター] - 人工知能（ＡＩ）開発企業アンソロピックと医療情報プラットフォームのオープンエビデンスは２２日、ＡＩを活用した臨床意思決定支援ツールを中低所得国の医師に提供するため提携すると発表した。

オープンエビデンスは査読済みの医学研究や治療ガイドラインを基に医師の質問に回答するサービス。米国と欧州の臨床医は無料で利用できる。

新たな取り組みでは、医学文献や専門家の知見、継続的医学教育へのアクセスが限られ患者ケアに支障が出かねない数十の中低所得国で医療従事者に特化版を無償で提供する。

オープンエビデンスが示したリストによると、この取り組みはウガンダ、アンゴラ、スーダン、ハイチ、モンゴルなど約１００カ国で展開する。

両社によると、アンソロピックの技術がバックエンドの基盤を提供し、オープンエビデンスが医療インフラを踏まえて地域ごとにシステムを最適化する。

提携に関する金銭面の条件は明らかにしていない。

ロイターは先週、アンソロピックがＡＩ技術を応用した医薬品開発の本格化に向け、生物学の研究を行うための研究所を設立したと報じた。

item.title: China surveys Broadcom switch use in state data centers, FT reports
item.description: Chinese authorities are examining the use of Broadcom’s hardware in state-backed data centres as part of a drive to boost domestic producers and reduce reliance on foreign AI infrastructure, the Financial Times reported Wednesday, citing people familiar with the matter.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Chinese authorities are examining the use of Broadcom’s (AVGO.O) hardware in state-backed data centres as part of a drive to boost domestic producers and reduce reliance on foreign AI infrastructure, the Financial Times reported Wednesday, citing people familiar with the matter. Amid rivalry with the US, China has sharpened its [USN:L1N44V0AA TEXT:"focus"] on technological self-sufficiency and supply-chain resilience and provided particular support for smaller specialised companies it calls little giants. The State-owned Assets Supervision and Administration Commission (SASAC), which oversees state-owned enterprises, has spent recent weeks surveying how extensively Broadcom's switches are deployed across state-controlled data centres, the report said. Reuters could not immediately verify the report. Broadcom and SASAC could not be immediately reached for comment outside regular business hours. The survey found that Broadcom switches could account for as much as 90% of the equipment in use, the report added. Based on those preliminary findings, SASAC may issue informal guidance directing state-run data centres to scale back their use of Broadcom switches as part of Beijing's "domestic chips for domestic use" campaign — an effort to expand adoption of Chinese-made semiconductors and AI technology across the public sector, the newspaper reported. Broadcom, along with Nvidia (NVDA.O) and China's Huawei, sells high-end switches within the country. Although Nvidia products have already been barred from state-backed data centres, Broadcom's switches remain widely present in these facilities, the report added.

item.title: ベネズエラ野党指導者、帰国の試み失敗 暫定大統領は米大統領と会談
item.description: [２２日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[２２日 ロイター] - ベネズエラの野党指導者マリア・コリナ・マチャド氏は、過去２４時間の間に３回にわたりベネズエラへの帰国を試みたが、いずれも失敗に終わったと、同氏のチームが２２日に明らかにしたほか、メディアが伝えた。一方、ベネズエラのロドリゲス暫定大統領はこの日、国連総会が開かれているニューヨークでトランプ米大統領と会談した。

ロドリゲス氏は、暫定大統領就任後初めて米国を訪問。今年１月の米軍によるマドゥロ大統領の身柄拘束後、初の首脳会談となった。

スペイン紙ＡＢＣの報道によると、マチャド氏の顧問ペドロ・ウルチュルトゥ氏はソーシャルメディアで、マチャド氏が９カ月前に密かにベネズエラを出国して以降、失敗に終わった帰国の試みは７回に上り、今回の海路と空路による試みもこれに含まれると述べた。

この発言は後にマチャド氏の広報担当者によって確認された。マチャド氏自身は、失敗した試みについて公に言及していない。

米国務省はロイターのコメント要請に直ちに応じなかった。

関係者によると、６月にベネズエラで発生した地震を受け、米当局者は非公式にマチャド氏に帰国の延期を促し、同氏の帰国の試みに反対した。

ＡＢＣは、海路と空路での帰国の試みを誰が阻止したのかについて詳細を伝えていない。

item.title: Royal Caribbean acquires stake in resort operator Sandals for $3 billion
item.description: Royal Caribbean Group said on Wednesday it had agreed to acquire a 50% stake in Caribbean resorts operator Sandals Resorts International for $3 billion, expanding the cruise company's presence in land-based vacation experiences.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Royal Caribbean Group (RCL.N) said on Wednesday it had agreed to acquire a 50% stake in Caribbean resorts operator Sandals Resorts International for $3 billion, expanding the cruise company's presence in land-based vacation experiences. Royal Caribbean has been focused on broadening its land-based vacation offerings, including its Royal Beach Club private destinations and Perfect Day destinations, as cruise operators seek to capture a larger share of consumers' overall travel spending. The deal, expected to close in early 2027, would add Sandals' 20 resorts to Royal Caribbean's portfolio and broaden its exposure to travelers who prefer resort stays over cruises. Sandals, founded in 1981 by the late Gordon "Butch" Stewart, operates all-inclusive resorts across the Caribbean under the Sandals and Beaches brands with properties in Jamaica, the Bahamas, Saint Lucia, Grenada, Barbados, and other destinations. Royal Caribbean Group said it has secured committed debt financing from Morgan Stanley to fund the investment. The Financial Times first reported this week that the deal could value Sandals at more than $6 billion, citing people familiar with the matter. Sandals has been the subject of speculation about a potential sale for nearly a decade. Reuters reported in 2017 that the company was exploring strategic alternatives, including a sale, citing people familiar with the matter. A board jointly led by Jason Liberty, chairman and CEO of Royal Caribbean Group, and Adam Stewart, executive chairman of Sandals Resorts, will oversee the joint venture. Stewart will remain executive chairman of Sandals and Beaches Resorts and continue to oversee the brands' long-term growth strategy. Sandals faced controversy in the early 2000s over a policy that barred same-sex couples from its couples-only resorts. The company dropped the policy in 2004 after the London Underground banned its advertisements following complaints from gay rights activists.

item.title: Elections législatives au Maroc sur fond de désillusion de la jeunesse
item.description: Les Marocains sont appelés aux urnes mercredi pour des élections législatives sans grand enjeu dans un contexte de difficultés économiques et de désillusion de la jeunesse.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Les Marocains sont appelés aux urnes mercredi pour des élections législatives sans grand enjeu dans un contexte de difficultés économiques et de désillusion de la jeunesse. Le scrutin devrait globalement laisser l'équilibre des pouvoirs inchangé au Maroc, où le roi conserve des pouvoirs étendus en matière d'orientation politique, de défense et d'affaires étrangères. Le prochain Parlement aura toutefois pour mission de mettre en oeuvre des initiatives visant de plus en plus à répondre au mécontentement de la [USN:L6N4590UA TEXT:"jeunesse"], largement impliquée dans les importantes manifestations en 2025 et l'afflux massif de Marocains vers l'enclave espagnole de [USN:L8N43X1D1 TEXT:"Ceuta"] en juillet. Le gouvernement actuel est composé de trois partis – dont deux fondés par des hommes proches de la royauté – qui ont évincé un parti islamiste modéré arrivé au pouvoir une décennie plus tôt, après les manifestations du Printemps arabe de 2011. Les manifestations de 2011 avaient conduit le roi à déléguer davantage de pouvoirs au Parlement, avant de réaffirmer ensuite son contrôle sur des domaines tels que les affaires étrangères et le ministère de l'Intérieur. En vertu de la Constitution adoptée en 2011, le roi nomme le Premier ministre issu du parti ayant remporté la plus grande part des 395 sièges du Parlement. Le Premier ministre doit ensuite négocier la formation d'une coalition avant de soumettre une liste des membres du gouvernement à l'approbation royale. Les bureaux de vote ouvriront à 08h00 et fermeront 19h00. Les résultats préliminaires sont généralement annoncés le lendemain du scrutin. Le taux de participation, en particulier chez les jeunes électeurs, sera suivi de près, car il sera considéré comme un baromètre de l'engagement des citoyens et de leur confiance dans les institutions. Environ 27 millions de Marocains sont en âge de voter, mais seuls 15,8 millions sont inscrits sur les listes électorales, soit une baisse d'environ 12% par rapport aux élections de 2021. Le nouveau gouvernement supervisera également les dernières étapes d'un programme de 20 milliards de dollars visant à préparer la Coupe du monde 2030 de football, que le Maroc co-organisera avec l'Espagne et le Portugal.

item.title: German and Dutch strategic innovation agencies to collaborate on AI chip design
item.description: A new Dutch government agency set up to achieve strategic innovation will work with its German counterpart to pursue breakthroughs in AI computer chip design, it said on Wednesday, as part of European efforts to reduce reliance on US expertise.
item.dc:creator: Toby Sterling
item.content:encoded: A new Dutch government agency set up to achieve strategic innovation will work with its German counterpart to pursue breakthroughs in AI computer chip design, it said on Wednesday, as part of European efforts to reduce reliance on US expertise. The National Agency for Disruptive Innovation, or NADI for short, was set up this month with €500 million ($570 million) of government money as a Dutch equivalent of the US Defense Advanced Research Projects Agency. Popularly known as DARPA, that agency was set up in 1958 in response to the Soviet Union's Sputnik launch and played a role in the technologies that led to the internet, stealth aircraft and GPS. DRAWING ON ASML ECOSYSTEM Co-founder of NADI, Jelle Prins, said that a partnership with Germany on chips was natural, given the strong ecosystem around equipment maker ASML (ASML.AS) in the Netherlands, and German strengths in research and manufacturing. In the project, NADI and German counterpart, SPRIND, will commit €40 million over 20 months to groups of small teams using AI to accelerate the design of chips for training and "inference", or running, AI models. Prins said NVIDIA chips are powerful but inefficient for inference tasks, comparing them to "doing your shopping with a truck" rather than a grocery cart. In Europe, France established its defence innovation agency AID in 2018, Germany set up SPRIND in 2019 and Britain launched ARIA in 2023. France's AID backed development of remote-controlled munitions capable of destroying armoured targets at a 50-km (30-mile) distance that are entering procurement by the French military. SPRIND is separately running a €125 million challenge aimed at creating three European frontier-AI labs. SPRIND’s head of challenges, Jano Costard, told Reuters the goal with chips was to achieve “several orders of magnitude acceleration” in a design process that currently takes years. ($1 = 0.8731 euros)

item.title: H&M founding family builds stake as turnaround struggles to gain traction
item.description: The billionaire family behind H&M is quietly increasing its stake, fuelling speculation it could take the fast-fashion retailer private as CEO Daniel Erver's turnaround efforts have so far failed to boost the shares or lift sales significantly.
item.dc:creator: Greta Fondahn, Helen Reid
item.content:encoded: The billionaire family behind H&M (HMb.ST) is quietly increasing its stake, fuelling speculation it could take the fast-fashion retailer private as CEO Daniel Erver's turnaround efforts have so far failed to boost the shares or lift sales significantly. The Persson family's Ramsbury Invest holding company, primarily owned by Sweden's richest person Stefan Persson, has bought 36.8 million H&M shares so far this year, regulatory filings show. Stefan Persson is the son of H&M founder Erling Persson and the father of chairman Karl-Johan Persson. The family and related entities owned more than 68% of H&M's shares at the end of August, according to the company's website, up from 49.5% at the start of 2021. "It is very difficult to view it any other way than that their strategy is to slowly buy out the company," said Sverre Linton, chief legal officer of the Swedish Shareholders' Association, which represents small shareholders. "You could call it Sweden's slowest buyout." Under Swedish rules, shareholders who own 90% of a company can compel the purchase of the remaining shares. Minority shareholders would be best served either by a successful turnaround that lifts H&M's share price or by a "decent" cash offer from the Persson family, Linton said. "I believe there are many shareholders who would be willing to accept such an offer at this stage." Deutsche Bank analyst Adam Cochrane expects the family to take H&M private by 2030. H&M referred questions about the share purchases to Ramsbury Invest, where a spokesperson declined to comment on any plans to take the company private, saying only: "The Persson family believes in the company, are long-term owners and have historically increased their ownership over time." STUCK IN THE MIDDLE H&M has struggled to lift sales as shoppers have cut back on spending and competition has intensified from ultra-cheap online retailers such as Shein (0625.HK) and from Zara owner Inditex (ITX.MC) . The stock has lost more than 50% of its value since peaking in 2015. Erver took over as CEO in January 2024 with a mandate to improve profitability and strengthen the brand, but has yet to reignite sales growth. Sales fell 1% in the first quarter and were flat in the second. Analysts expect only modest growth in the third quarter, which H&M reports on Thursday. "Maybe the family feels that they get so much negative feedback from the markets, it's better for them to just be outside the market and then they can go ahead with much more long-term strategies," said Peter Magnusson, a portfolio manager at Cicero Fonder in Stockholm, who also expects the Perssons to take H&M private.

item.title: Astros slug 3 homers, blank Mariners to pull even in AL West
item.description: Christian Walker hit a three-run home run, Yordan Alvarez launched a two-run homer and Isaac Paredes added a solo shot as the visiting Houston Astros slugged their way to a 7-0 victory over the Seattle Mariners on Tuesday.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Christian Walker hit a three-run home run, Yordan Alvarez launched a two-run homer and Isaac Paredes added a solo shot as the visiting Houston Astros slugged their way to a 7-0 victory over the Seattle Mariners on Tuesday. Jose Altuve, Yainer Diaz, Alvarez and Paredes each collected two hits for the Astros (78-79), who pulled into a first-place tie with the Texas Rangers in the American League West. Houston owns the head-to-head tiebreaker over Texas, so would win the division if the teams remain tied at the end of the season. Five Astros pitchers combined to throw a four-hit shutout. Miguel Ullola (1-0) earned his first major league win, allowing one hit and striking out two over two innings. Julio Rodriguez notched two hits for Seattle (73-84). The Mariners went 0-for-3 with runners in scoring position and stranded nine. Jeremy Pena led off the game with an infield single to shortstop, stole second, and scored on Alvarez's single to right. It marked the 100th RBI of the season for Alvarez, the second time in his career he's reached that milestone. Paredes and Altuve followed with singles, loading the bases with no outs. Seattle starter Logan Gilbert (12-11) escaped the first-inning jam when Diaz struck out looking before Walker and Taylor Trammell flied out. Altuve and Diaz opened the third with back-to-back singles before Walker launched his 26th home run of the season and the 200th of his career, a three-run shot to deep left, giving the Astros a 4-0 lead. In the fifth, J.P. Crawford drew a one-out walk. After Randy Arozarena struck out swinging, Dominic Canzone singled to center. Crawford advanced to third, but Cal Raleigh struck out to end the inning. Houston's advantage increased to 5-0 on Paredes' solo homer in the sixth. With one out in the eighth, Pena was hit by a pitch, and Alvarez belted a slider over the wall in right for his 41st home run of the season, extending Houston's lead to 7-0. Houston starter Cristian Javier tossed two shutout innings, allowing one hit and two walks while striking out two. The Astros announced Javier exited the game with groin tightness. Gilbert gave up four runs on 10 hits over four innings, walking two and striking out three. --Field Level Media

item.title: Private equity firm EQT launches Middle East platform, opens Abu Dhabi office
item.description: Swedish private equity firm EQT is launching a Middle East platform, it said on Wednesday as it opened an office in Abu Dhabi, establishing an on-the-ground presence in the Gulf and joining a slew of firms that have expanded in the region in recent years.
item.dc:creator: Federico Maccioni
item.content:encoded: Swedish private equity firm EQT (EQTAB.ST) is launching a Middle East platform, it said on Wednesday as it opened an office in Abu Dhabi, establishing an on-the-ground presence in the Gulf and joining a slew of firms that have expanded in the region in recent years. The platform will deepen support for EQT's existing portfolio companies, build on its institutional relationships in the region and pursue new investment opportunities, the company said in a statement. Jimmy Mahtani, who was appointed chairman of the company's Gulf operations, leads the platform, while its office in Abu Dhabi's financial centre is led by Middle East head Smiyet Belrhiti. The office will also welcome a team spanning private capital and infrastructure investment alongside capital raising and business operations. EQT has $389 billion in assets under management. Its portfolio companies with an active presence in the Gulf region include Nord Anglia Education. Global investment firms have increased their Gulf footprint, lured by proximity to some of the world's largest sovereign wealth funds. They are also attracted by a growing pipeline of deals as regional governments diversify away from hydrocarbon revenue. The [USN:L6N43I0RJ TEXT:"inflow"] comes amid the Middle East conflict , which has brought turmoil, with heavy disruption to travel and supply chains. “The launch of EQT's Middle East platform reflects our conviction in the scale and momentum of opportunity across the GCC (Gulf Cooperation Council)," EQT CEO and Managing Partner Per Franzén said. Abu Dhabi is home to the vast majority of the United Arab Emirates' oil reserves and its sovereign funds are estimated to collectively manage over $1.8 trillion in assets. The number of financial services entities operating from Abu Dhabi's financial centre rose 27% in the first half of the year to 392.

item.title: Musk praises Xi as great leader in interview with Chinese state television
item.description: Tesla Inc CEO Elon Musk praised Chinese President Xi Jinping as a "great leader" in comments during an interview with Chinese state television network CCTV on Wednesday.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Tesla Inc CEO Elon Musk praised Chinese President Xi Jinping as a "great leader" in comments during an interview with Chinese state television network CCTV on Wednesday. "Under his tenure, China has prospered immensely," Musk said, citing progress seen from new buildings and infrastructure constructed in the country. "It's also obvious to see that, just walking around the streets, the increased prosperity of the average Chinese citizen," he added. Musk was expected to join other US chief executives at a White House state dinner hosted by President Donald Trump for Xi on Thursday, Reuters [USN:L1N45E0J5 TEXT:"reported"]. Xi is due to meet with Trump on Thursday in the [USN:L8N45A068 TEXT:"second summit"] this year between the leaders of the world's two largest economies. Musk also commented on Tesla's largest manufacturing hub, which is located in Shanghai, calling the team "incredibly talented, hardworking and trustworthy". "Tesla's Shanghai factory is a gem and it's beautiful, actually, if anyone's ever been there," he said. Musk had previously dismissed [USN:L6N44110R TEXT:"speculation"] that Tesla's China operations could be separated ahead of a potential merger with SpaceX. Sales of Model 3 and Model Y vehicles produced at Tesla's Shanghai plant, also its largest export hub globally, rose 3.6% year-on-year in August, [USN:L1N44U0EP TEXT:"slowing"] sharply from the previous month, as divergent trends persisted across the US automaker's major markets.

item.title: Gold lacklustre as higher-for-longer rate outlook weighs on sentiment
item.description: Gold prices fell on Wednesday as investors weighed the prospect of major central banks keeping interest rates elevated for longer in their efforts to curb persistent inflation.
item.dc:creator: Ashitha Shivaprasad
item.content:encoded: Gold prices fell on Wednesday as investors weighed the prospect of major central banks keeping interest rates elevated for longer in their efforts to curb persistent inflation. Spot gold fell 0.6% to $4,329.31 per ounce, as of 0623 GMT. US gold futures for December delivery were down 0.2% at $4,366.90. The dollar rose to its strongest level in two months. A firmer dollar makes greenback-priced bullion more expensive for overseas buyers. "Short-term volatility in gold very much depends on how oil trades and the developments that happen in the Middle East. However, long-term structural drivers for gold are still really strong," said Kyle Rodda, senior financial market analyst at Capital.com. While bullion is often seen as a safeguard against inflation, its appeal tends to wane when elevated rates boost returns on interest-bearing investments. US President Donald Trump [USN:L8N45E0CI TEXT:"warned"] that he could annihilate Iran if there is no deal to end the war, but also suggested an agreement could come soon amid a diplomatic push at the United Nations. Boston Federal Reserve President [USN:L6N45E0OR TEXT:"Susan Collins"] wrote in a Linkedin post that she supported the US central bank's decision last week to raise interest rates in the face of risks that future inflation will be above the 2% target. Collins, who is not a voting member of the rate-setting Federal Open Market Committee this year, did not say if she wants rates to go up again. The Fed last week lifted its benchmark rate by 25 basis points to 3.75%-4.00% and signalled another increase could come before year-end. The [USN:L1N459138 TEXT:"Bank of Japan"] and the [USN:L1N45E0X1 TEXT:"European Central Bank"] have also raised rates recently. Analysts at BMI maintained their 2026 gold price forecast at an average of $4,400 per ounce, noting that elevated geopolitical risks and continued central bank purchases are expected to ensure a strong floor under gold around the $3,800 level. Among other metals, spot silver fell 1.2% to $66.24 per ounce, platinum lost 1.4% to $1,807.80 and palladium declined 1.1% at $1,293.68.

item.title: 台湾、計画通りの武器売却に向け米と「緊密な連携」維持へ
item.description: [台南（台湾） ２３日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
[台南（台湾） ２３日 ロイター] - 台湾国防部（国防省）の当局者は２３日、計画通りに台湾への武器売却が進むよう、引き続き米国と緊密に連携していくと述べた。米ワシントンでは２４日に米中首脳会談が予定されている。

中国は台湾を自国の領土と見なしており、米国に対し、台湾への武器売却の中止を繰り返し要求してきた。

トランプ米大統領は昨年１２月、台湾向けとして過去最大規模となる１１０億ドルの武器売却パッケージを承認したが、今年５月に北京を訪問した後、約１４０億ドル規模の第２弾のパッケージは保留中だと述べた。

２４日の米中首脳会談では、中国の習近平国家主席がトランプ大統領に対し、武器売却の中止を強く求めるものとみられる。

台湾国防部の副報道官は記者団に対し、インド太平洋地域の安全保障と安定の維持は「民主主義諸国の共通の利益」だとし、「米国政府と議会は台湾の自衛能力に対する支持を繰り返し表明してきた」と語った。「したがって、われわれは引き続き米国防総省と緊密な連絡を取り、計画通りに武器売却の実施を推進していく」と述べた。

台湾の頼清徳総統は、同盟国に防衛費の増額を求めるトランプ氏の呼びかけに賛同している。

item.title: 中国、フェンタニル関連犯罪の指針公表 米中首脳会談控え
item.description: ［北京 ２３日 ロイター］ -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
［北京　２３日　ロイター］ - 中国の司法・公安当局は２３日、フェンタニル関連物質が絡む刑事事件を適切に取り締まるための指針を公表した。

習近平国家主席は２４日にワシントンでトランプ米大統領と首脳会談を行う。トランプ政権は、合成麻薬フェンタニルの原料となる化学物質の米国流入阻止に向けた対策強化を中国側に再三要請している。２２日には中国商務省が、薬物原料となる化学物質の輸出管理リストに２種類追加したと発表した。

中国最高人民法院、最高人民検察院、公安省の共同声明によると、指針は有罪認定と量刑に関する数量基準を明確化することを目的とし、対象物質を医薬品と非医薬品に分類する。

密輸、売買、輸送、製造、不法所持のほか、インターネットを利用した関連犯罪についても当局が捜査する。

item.title: 高市首相、米中首脳会談念頭にトランプ氏と意見交換 ＩＣＣでもやり取り
item.description:
Tamiyuki Kihara
[２３日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Tamiyuki Kihara

[２３日 ロイター] - 高市早苗首相は２３日、国連総会出席のため訪問中の米国で記者会見を開き、前日の日米首脳会談で「トランプ米大統領と米中首脳会談を念頭に中国をめぐる諸課題についてタイムリーに意見交換した」と述べた。トランプ氏と中国の習近平国家主席との会談は２４日に予定されており、日本はその前に米との首脳会談を模索していた。

高市、トランプ両氏は現地時間２２日に会談した。高市氏は記者会見で、トランプ氏と経済安全保障、人工知能（ＡＩ）、半導体、重要鉱物などにおける協力を一層強化することで一致したと説明。「このタイミングでの会談は、日米同盟の強さを世界に示すものになったと確信している」と述べた。

また、米中首脳会談を控え、中国についても意見交換したとし、「米中関係が日本を含む国際社会の安定に資するものとなることが重要だ」と語った。中国と台湾の関係をめぐる日本側からの要望の有無など、詳細については明らかにしなかった。

一方、トランプ氏が批判を強める国際刑事裁判所（ＩＣＣ）については、日本が国際社会における法の支配を徹底するため「ＩＣＣを一貫して支持している」と強調。トランプ氏ともこの点について「率直にやり取りを行った」と述べた。

記者団からイラン情勢について質問を受けると、「法の支配に基づく海洋秩序が大きく揺らいでいることを強く懸念している」と表明。中東地域全体の事態の早期沈静化や安定化が何よりも重要だとし、ホルムズ海峡については追加的な費用がない形で自由で安全な航行が一刻も早く回復されることの重要性を指摘した。

米ホワイトハウスは日米首脳会談について、ソーシャルメディアに会談時の写真を掲載。「トランプ大統領と日本の高市早苗首相が国連総会にて、米国と日本の強固な同盟関係をさらに深めている」と発信した。

高市氏は２２日、ウクライナのゼレンスキー大統領とも会談した。高市氏は会見で、今年の冬に向けてエネルギー分野を含めた支援を表明し、対ロ制裁を継続する考えをゼレンスキー氏に伝えたと説明した。

（鬼原民幸　編集：久保信博）

Sept 23 : New Zealand fast bowler Adam Milne and spin all-rounder Michael Bracewell have returned to a 16-member squad for next month's Twenty20 home series against India, the country's cricket board (NZC) said on Wednesday. • New Zealand host India in five T20s, five one-day internationals (ODIs) and two tests, with the opening T20 in Christchurch on October 22. • Thirteen members of the squad that finished runners-up to India at this year's T20 World Cup have been retained, with Bracewell and Milne returning after missing the tournament through injury. • Rachin Ravindra, who dislocated his right shoulder during a promotional shoot last week, has been ruled out of the T20 series but is expected to return for the ODIs.

item.title: 米共和党上院議員、トランプ一族の事業取引巡り調査要求
item.description:
Susan Heavey
[ワシントン ２２日 ロイター] -
item.dc:creator: ロイター
item.content:encoded:
Susan Heavey

[ワシントン ２２日 ロイター] - 米共和党のジョン・カーティス上院議員（ユタ州選出）は２２日、トランプ大統領の家族が同氏の在任中に利益を得ているかどうかについて調査を行うよう求めた。また、大統領一族が立場を悪用しているという印象は政府への信頼を損なうと述べた。

カーティス議員は上院司法委員会宛ての書簡で、トランプ氏の長男ジュニア氏が所有する企業や、今年バハマで行われた同氏の結婚祝賀会に対するロシアのオリガルヒ（新興財閥）からの支払いを調査するよう求めた。連邦議会の民主党議員らは先週、この結婚式の支払いに関する調査を開始している。

上院司法委のチャック・グラスリー委員長は記者団に対し、この要請を真剣に検討すると述べたものの、調査の可否を決定するには時間がかかるとした。決定は１１月３日の中間選挙が終わるまでは下されない見通しだ。

中間選挙が迫る中、有力な共和党議員の一部には、支持率が低下の一途をたどる大統領との距離を置こうとする動きが見られる。ただ、書簡を送ったカーティス議員は２０３０年まで選挙を控えていない。

カーティス氏は上院司法委に対し、大統領一家の人間関係や、国内外の団体による影響力の行使の可能性について調査するよう求めた。これには、ロシアのオリガルヒであるウマル・クレムレフ氏が支払ったジュニア氏の結婚祝賀会の費用、数十万ドルも含まれる。

カーティス氏はまた、父親の大統領在任中にジュニア氏が行っている、仮想通貨の宣伝、不動産取引、予測市場プラットフォームなどのビジネス活動についても疑問を呈した。

カーティス氏は「これらの報道は、現職大統領の家族に対する外国勢力のアクセスおよびそのような関係が有利な扱いを受けるという実際の、あるいは見かけ上の期待を生み出す可能性があるかについて正当な疑問を提起している」とした上で、「それらは見返りを期待させる可能性もあり、それは国家安全保障上の脆弱性さえも生み出す恐れがある」と指摘した。

トランプ氏は先週、ジュニア氏がクレムレフ氏への支払いを返済中だと述べたが、それ以上の詳細は明かさなかった。

トランプ一家はトランプ氏の在任中における家族のビジネス取引を擁護し、ジュニア氏と別の息子エリック氏が管理する信託を根拠に、いかなる利益相反もないと否定している。

ジュニア氏の代理人はコメント要請に応じなかった。

item.title: Taiwan to maintain 'close contact' with US on arms sales
item.description: Taiwan will continue to keep in close touch with the US to promote the implementation of arms sales according to plan, a defence ministry official said on Wednesday, ahead of a meeting between the US and Chinese leaders in Washington.
item.dc:creator: Fabian Hamacher, Tsai Hsin-Han
item.content:encoded: Taiwan will continue to keep in close touch with the US to promote the implementation of arms sales according to plan, a defence ministry official said on Wednesday, ahead of a meeting between the US and Chinese leaders in Washington. China views democratically governed Taiwan as its own territory and has repeatedly demanded US arms sales end. While US President Donald Trump approved an $11 billion package for Taiwan in December, the largest ever, he said in May after visiting Beijing that a second package, worth some $14 billion, was being kept in [USN:L1N41S025 TEXT:"abeyance"]. Chinese President Xi Jinping is expected to press Trump to [USN:L1N45E095 TEXT:"halt sales"] when the two of them meet in Washington this week. Speaking to reporters in southern Taiwan's Tainan during a media trip, Taiwan defence ministry deputy spokesperson Chiao Fu-chun said maintaining security and stability in the Indo-Pacific region was a "common interest of democratic nations". "The US government and Congress have repeatedly expressed their support for Taiwan's ability to defend itself," he added. "Therefore, we will continue to maintain close contact with the US Department of War and continue to promote the implementation of arms sales according to plan." In separate comments in the neighbouring city of Kaohsiung, Taiwan Premier Cho Jung-tai said he had "deep confidence" in the future of relations with the US. Taiwan President Lai Ching-te has embraced Trump's call for US allies to spend more on their [USN:L4N44U0EB TEXT:"defence"]. While the US is Taiwan's most important arms supplier, Taipei has its own weapons development programme, covering everything from submarines and fighter jets to long-range missiles. Taiwan's army on Wednesday showed off its new eight-wheeled armoured combat vehicle fitted with a 105mm gun, practising live fire exercises to demonstrate the domestically made weapon's fighting abilities. The military also put on display, but did not fire, some of its US-made weapons, such as Lockheed Martin-made (LMT.N) HIMARS rockets. Taiwan routinely holds live fire drills and takes reporters to military bases and to watch exercises. China has never renounced the use of force to bring Taiwan under its control, and its military operates around the island on an almost daily basis. Taiwan's government rejects Beijing's sovereignty claims, saying only the Taiwanese people can decide their future.

LONDON, Sept 23 : Alexander Zverev has revealed to rival Carlos Alcaraz what was going through his head as he served for the US Open title in New York earlier this month — absolutely nothing. Zverev secured his first title at Flushing Meadows with a four-set victory over Ben Shelton but returned to the baseline as if to prepare for another game after his American opponent hit long on championship point. "I thought it was 4-1," Zverev said after Alcaraz quizzed him about the moment as the Team Europe teammates prepared for the Laver Cup on Tuesday. "If it were 5-2, I'd have been so nervous, for sure.

item.title: Trump meets Venezuela’s Delcy Rodriguez for the first time since Maduro’s capture
item.description: The meeting came during Rodriguez's first trip to the US since taking office. She is set to address the General Assembly Wednesday afternoon.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded:
